Definition: the figure or person (as if cut out); also an inclosure (as separated)
BiblicalUsage: gizrâh is the word for a separate place, a cutting. In Ezekiel 41:12, the text says "Now the building that [was] before the separate place at the end toward the west [was] seventy cubits broad." In Ezekiel 41:13, the text says "and the separate place."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that gizrâh matters because worship is not a performance but a response — we answer what God has done with what we are. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
